title: Strongest Signal
statement:
A radio telescope receives **n** signal codes, each a non-negative integer below 2^30. Combining two different signals i and j produces the value a[i] XOR a[j] (bitwise exclusive or: a bit of the result is 1 when exactly one of the two numbers has a 1 in that position).

Find the largest value of a[i] XOR a[j] over all pairs i < j.
input:
The first line contains an integer **n**.

The second line contains n integers a[1], ..., a[n].
output: Print one integer: the maximum XOR of two of the numbers.
hints: Trying all pairs is O(n^2): too slow for 10^5.
Build the answer bit by bit from the highest bit. A high bit is worth more than all lower bits together, so greedily try to make each bit 1.
Store all numbers in a binary trie (a tree with a 0-child and a 1-child for each bit). For each number walk down, preferring the opposite bit.
editorial:
Binary trie: insert all numbers bit by bit from bit 29 down to bit 0. For each number x, walk from the root and at every bit try to go to the child with the **opposite** bit (that makes the XOR bit 1); if it does not exist, follow the same bit. The value collected is the best partner for x. The maximum over all x is the answer.

Equivalent prefix-set method: decide the answer from the top bit down. For bit b, take the set of all numbers' top bits (prefixes); the bit can be 1 if some two prefixes XOR to (current answer with bit b set), checked with a hash set.

Complexity: O(30·n).
